caseStudy.title: NGIT Edu – High-Concurrency Examination & Typing Engine
caseStudy.subtitle: Eliminating keystroke lag and platform crashes for thousands of government exam aspirants across India.
caseStudy.overview: NGIT Edu is an established educational and certification institute preparing aspirants for competitive examinations requiring rigorous typing and computer literacy standards (such as Allahabad High Court ARO/RO, UP Police Computer Operator, SSC CHSL, and NIELIT CCC/O-Level). Prior to the architectural overhaul, peak test cycles with hundreds of concurrent users caused keystroke buffering delays, inaccurate WPM scoring, and server timeouts on legacy PHP infrastructure. Devraj Singh Tomar was brought in to architect a modern, sub-millisecond typing evaluation engine and server-rendered curriculum portal.

challenge.problem: Government typing examinations demand strict adherence to keystroke accuracy, backspace penalties, and font specificities (Mangal Remington Gail, Kruti Dev 010, and standard English QWERTY). Legacy desktop software was cumbersome to deploy on student hardware, while existing web alternatives suffered from noticeable keystroke event latency, inaccurate words-per-minute (WPM) calculations, and server crashes during sudden traffic surges when mock tests were published.
bottlenecks: Unacceptable 80ms-150ms input lag on browser textareas causing student typing errors.
Server-side evaluation models creating severe database thread locks under 500+ concurrent test takers.
Complex font mapping glitches when rendering bilingual Hindi (Mangal Unicode vs Kruti Dev ASCII) test passages.
Loss of test progress during intermittent student network dropouts.
challenge.whyExistingFailed: Generic off-the-shelf LMS platforms and WordPress plugins were built for static multiple-choice quizzes, completely lacking the low-level DOM event capture, raw keystroke telemetry, and offline event queues required for high-stakes speed typing evaluations.

solution.strategy: Engineered a distributed client-side evaluation engine built on Next.js and TypeScript, decoupling real-time keystroke processing from network roundtrips. All keystroke timing, error calculations, backspace accounting, and WPM velocity are computed locally inside an in-memory state machine and synced atomically at the conclusion of the test session.
architectureHighlights: Sub-millisecond client-side keyboard event listener bypassing standard textarea overhead.
Edge-cached passage banks with instant randomized test generation.
Dual Hindi font engine supporting both legacy Remington Gail / Mangal Unicode and Kruti Dev 010 mapping.
Atomic test submission payload with cryptographic tamper detection against client-side score modification.
keyDecisions: Adopted Next.js App Router for SSG/ISR static documentation and dynamic Edge API routes for mock evaluations.
Stored question passages at the CDN edge to guarantee sub-100ms first contentful paint (FCP).
Implemented local Web Storage state buffering so candidates can complete tests even during brief ISP disconnections.

myContribution.summary: Devraj Singh Tomar served as the Technical Architect & Lead Engine Developer, directly owning the typing engine's core mathematical logic, client-side event architecture, and cloud deployment pipeline.
responsibilities: Designed the core JavaScript/TypeScript typing engine algorithm with zero-lag keystroke evaluation.
Engineered the Hindi transliteration and font-swapping renderer for Mangal and Kruti Dev passages.
Architected serverless API endpoints on Next.js to verify and persist completed candidate test results.
Configured technical SEO metadata and structured schemas for high-intent search queries across Uttar Pradesh.
distinctions: Devraj personally authored the typing engine algorithms and frontend state machine.
Collaborated with NGIT faculty on official exam grading rules and passage validation.
Institute faculty provided subject matter materials, syllabus data, and question banks.

caseStudy.title: The Home Shifting – National Logistics Quote & Route Engine
caseStudy.subtitle: High-conversion moving and relocation platform engineered to dominate local search and maximize lead capture.
caseStudy.overview: The Home Shifting is an intercity relocation and logistics enterprise operating across 50+ major metropolitan corridors in India. In the intensely competitive packers and movers industry, companies spend thousands of rupees on digital ads, only to lose prospective customers because their mobile landing pages take over 4 seconds to load. Devraj Singh Tomar was brought on board as Full-Stack Performance Engineer to completely rebuild the digital acquisition platform, focusing on ultra-low latency, instant quote generation, and programmatic city-to-city landing page architecture.

challenge.problem: The client was experiencing a staggering 68% bounce rate on paid search campaigns. Mobile users searching for movers in cities like Delhi, Bangalore, Mumbai, and Lucknow were abandoning the platform before forms even rendered. Furthermore, the existing multi-step inquiry form asked for too many unnecessary fields upfront, causing prospective clients to seek estimates elsewhere.
bottlenecks: Unacceptable 4.2-second Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) on mobile Google Ads traffic.
Severe bounce rates resulting in wasted ad spend and low customer acquisition efficiency.
Lack of localized landing pages targeting specific origin-destination relocation routes.
Zero automated route distance or freight tier estimation.
challenge.whyExistingFailed: Generic WordPress themes loaded dozens of render-blocking JavaScript files, uncompressed hero sliders, and bloated visual page builders that devastated mobile Core Web Vitals.

solution.strategy: Engineered a purpose-built Next.js lead capture architecture featuring a 2-step dynamic quote estimator, programmatic static generation for 50+ regional hubs, sub-second LCP execution, and instant routing of leads directly to regional dispatch managers via WhatsApp Business API.
architectureHighlights: Sub-1-second mobile page loads achieving 95+ performance scores on Google Lighthouse.
Programmatic static generation for top intercity moving routes (e.g. Delhi to Bangalore, Mumbai to Pune).
Streamlined 2-step quote calculator asking only origin, destination, and inventory size.
Dynamic Google Maps route distance calculation and localized MovingCompany JSON-LD schema.
keyDecisions: Replaced bloated third-party form widgets with custom, zero-dependency lightweight React state forms.
Implemented instant server-side phone number validation to eliminate dummy quote requests.

caseStudy.overview: MAZ Dialysis Center in Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh, is recognized as the third largest specialized dialysis center in India, delivering life-saving renal care, peritoneal dialysis, and nephrology consultations to patients across Northern India. When dealing with end-stage renal disease (ESRD), families urgently need accurate machine availability, treatment scheduling, and immediate emergency contact. Devraj Singh Tomar partnered with center leadership to engineer a high-reliability, mobile-first healthcare portal optimized for instantaneous emergency triage, local Google 3-Pack authority, and dignified patient care.

challenge.problem: Patients requiring emergency dialysis cannot afford to navigate confusing menus or wait for slow-loading pages on poor rural 3G/4G connections. The center's previous lack of structured digital identity meant patients frequently called outdated numbers or struggled to verify accepted government schemes (Ayushman Bharat, CGHS). Furthermore, regional nephrology search queries on Google Maps and search were failing to surface the facility's immense infrastructure.
bottlenecks: Emergency patients unable to locate instant one-click calling or WhatsApp bed booking on mobile devices.
Lack of MedicalBusiness and MedicalProcedure schemas hurting Google local search rankings.
High bounce rate on slow-loading healthcare portals during critical decision windows.
Ambiguity regarding dialysis equipment standards, hygiene protocols, and visiting nephrologists.
challenge.whyExistingFailed: Standard medical templates are cluttered with generic stock photos and medical jargon, failing to address the acute, urgent needs of dialysis patients who need immediate machine availability verification and route navigation.

solution.strategy: Devraj architected a streamlined, high-contrast healthcare portal featuring a persistent emergency triage bar, verified infrastructure photo documentation, dynamic nephrology clinic schedules, and deep integration with Google Maps Local Schema. The portal highlights the facility's 50+ German-engineered dialysis stations and clean-room dialysis water purification systems.
architectureHighlights: Persistent mobile bottom bar providing one-tap emergency calling and direct WhatsApp triage dispatch.
MedicalBusiness and MedicalProcedure JSON-LD structured data embedding geographical coordinates and treatment offerings.
Optimized image delivery pipeline ensuring photos of clinical machines and ward hygiene load in under 500ms on 4G.
Dedicated Ayushman Bharat / PMJAY cashless treatment guidance pages with step-by-step document checklists.
keyDecisions: Prioritized mobile-first UX with high-contrast text sizing so elderly patients and stressed attendants can navigate effortlessly.
Integrated localized Google Business Profile sync to maintain consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) citations.
Implemented zero-friction appointment booking without requiring app downloads or account logins.

caseStudy.overview: T&S Lex Ink Legal is a premier New Delhi legal practice providing sophisticated corporate advisory, civil litigation, and criminal defense services. Legal institutions operate under rigorous regulatory boundaries (including Bar Council standards prohibiting overt advertising) and handle highly confidential corporate disclosures. Devraj Singh Tomar was engaged as Digital Architect and Security Consultant to engineer an authoritative, impenetrable digital facade that conveys institutional gravitas, enforces zero-trust confidentiality, and achieves flawless search engine indexing.

challenge.problem: The firm needed a contemporary digital presence that met three non-negotiable criteria: complete immunity from web vulnerabilities (XSS, CSRF, form injection), compliance with strict Bar Council professional conduct norms, and rapid search engine comprehension of their practice verticals (commercial dispute resolution, arbitration, white-collar defense, real estate law).
bottlenecks: Vulnerability risks associated with standard CMS platforms (WordPress/PHP plugins) exposing confidential consultation inquiries.
Slow, unoptimized legal directory templates creating poor mobile performance and bounce rates among corporate clients.
Lack of structured semantic data causing search engines to miss practice areas and credentialed advocate profiles.
Strict requirement for clean, un-spam-able consultation communication channels.
challenge.whyExistingFailed: Standard agency website templates rely on vulnerable third-party plugins, third-party form processors that store client data outside controlled jurisdictions, and bloated scripts that decimate performance.

solution.strategy: Architected a custom Next.js portal utilizing static generation and edge security headers. Devraj established a zero-trust form sanitization pipeline, implemented comprehensive Content Security Policies (CSP), and authored granular JSON-LD schemas representing the firm, its advocates, and specialized practice areas.
architectureHighlights: Strict Content Security Policy (CSP) blocking unauthorized scripts, clickjacking (frame-ancestors 'none'), and cross-site framing.
Sanitize-on-arrival contact form workflow with cryptographic honeypot filtering to eliminate automated bot spam.
Deep semantic SEO using Schema.org LegalService, Attorney, and WebSite microdata for instant algorithmic understanding.
100/100 Lighthouse performance across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO.

caseStudy.title: Divya Jap – Local-First Vedic Sadhana & Chanting Platform
caseStudy.subtitle: A digital Jap Mala and collective mantra meditation ecosystem engineered for deep spiritual practice.
caseStudy.overview: Divya Jap is a digital Vedic meditation and mantra japa companion engineered to preserve the sacred, tactile rhythm of a traditional 108-bead Jap Mala within a high-performance progressive web app. Devraj Singh Tomar conceptualized, architected, and built the application from the ground up, focusing on sensory feedback (haptics and resonant bell harmonics), zero-distraction dark mode ergonomics, privacy-first family chanting circles, and battery-efficient offline longevity.

challenge.problem: Devotees practicing daily japa found existing counter apps frustrating: aggressive visual ads shattered contemplative focus, apps required constant internet access that failed during remote temple pilgrimages or travel, and continuous screen illumination quickly drained mobile batteries. Furthermore, spiritual groups and families wishing to count collective chant commitments (e.g. 1.25 Lakh Mahamrityunjaya or Gayatri Japa) had no secure, privacy-preserving way to aggregate scores.
bottlenecks: Unreliable touch feedback forcing users to look at the screen rather than focusing inward.
Excessive battery consumption caused by unoptimized render loops during hour-long sessions.
Total data loss if a phone died or went offline during meditation sessions.
Privacy concerns with mainstream apps demanding intrusive phone permissions and social logins.
challenge.whyExistingFailed: Most digital counter apps on app stores are generic tally clickers wrapped in ad networks, lacking any spiritual design philosophy, sacred audio ergonomics, or architectural resilience for offline chanting.

solution.strategy: Architected an ultra-lightweight, local-first Progressive Web Application (PWA) using Next.js, Web Audio API, and Navigator Haptics. The app functions entirely offline, persists every count transaction immediately to IndexedDB/LocalState, and provides distinct vibration signatures for each bead tap and 108-bead Mala cycle completion.
architectureHighlights: Web Audio synthesized Tibetan singing bowl frequencies (108Hz resonance harmonics) generated client-side without heavy MP3 asset downloads.
